stem: The circumference of a circle is 10π. What is the area of the circle?
explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 10π gives r = 5, so the area is πr² = 25π. The choice 100π uses the diameter 10 as the radius, and 10π repeats the circumference.

stem: In the circle with center O shown, the radius is 10 and angle AOB measures 72°. What is the length of minor arc AB?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="112" r="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="150" y1="112" x2="236.9" y2="88.7" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="112" x2="154.7" y2="22.1" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="146" y="132" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="248.9" y="90.7" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="154.7" y="14.1" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="171.4" y="85.6" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">72°</text><text x="197.5" y="118.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text></svg>
explanation: An arc is the same fraction of the circumference as its central angle is of 360°. Here 72/360 = 1/5, and the circumference is 2π × 10 = 20π, so the arc is 20π/5 = 4π. The choice 20π is the whole circumference (and also the sector's area, (1/5) × 100π), not the arc length.

stem: The rectangular box shown has length 12, width 4 and height 3. What is the length of a diagonal of the box joining two opposite corners (shown as a dashed segment)?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="30,105 210,105 210,180 30,180" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="30" y1="105" x2="90" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="105" x2="270" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="180" x2="270" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="60" x2="270" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="270" y1="60" x2="270" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="135" x2="90" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="90" y1="135" x2="270" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="30" y1="180" x2="90" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="30" y1="180" x2="270" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="120" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text><text x="18" y="147" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="262" y="168" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
explanation: First find the diagonal of the 12-by-4 base: √(144 + 16) = √160. That segment and the height 3 are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the box's diagonal: √(160 + 9) = √169 = 13. In one step: √(12² + 4² + 3²) = 13. Using only two of the dimensions gives a face diagonal, which is shorter.

stem: What is the volume of the right circular cylinder shown, which has radius 3 and height 8?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><ellipse cx="150" cy="45" rx="70" ry="20" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="80" y1="45" x2="80" y2="175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="220" y1="45" x2="220" y2="175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M 80 175 A 70 20 0 0 0 220 175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><path d="M 80 175 A 70 20 0 0 1 220 175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="150" y1="45" x2="220" y2="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="185" y="41" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="236" y="115" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text></svg>
explanation: Volume = πr²h = π × 3² × 8 = 72π. The choice 48π is the curved (lateral) surface area 2πrh, 66π is the total surface area 2πr² + 2πrh, and 288π uses the diameter 6 in place of the radius.

stem: In the figure, O is the center of the circle and angle AOB measures 110°. What is the measure of angle ACB?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="112" r="92" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="150" y1="112" x2="63.5" y2="143.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="112" x2="209.1" y2="182.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="158" y1="20.4" x2="63.5" y2="143.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="158" y1="20.4" x2="209.1" y2="182.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="152" y="102" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="51.5" y="151.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="219.1" y="194.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="158" y="12.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="141.2" y="144.8" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">110°</text></svg>
explanation: Angle ACB is an inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc AB as the central angle AOB, so it is half as large: 110/2 = 55°. The choice 125° is half of the other arc (360 − 110 = 250), which would apply only if C were on minor arc AB; 220° doubles instead of halving.

stem: In the xy-plane, what is the distance between the points (−2, 3) and (4, −5)?
explanation: The horizontal change is 4 − (−2) = 6 and the vertical change is −5 − 3 = −8, so the distance is √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10. The choice 14 adds the two changes (walking along the grid), and 2√2 comes from a sign slip, using 4 − 2 and −5 + 3.

stem: In the xy-plane, what is the midpoint of the segment joining (1, 7) and (9, −3)?
explanation: The midpoint averages the coordinates: ((1 + 9)/2, (7 + (−3))/2) = (5, 2). The choice (4, −5) halves the differences instead of averaging, (8, −10) is the full difference, and (10, 4) adds without dividing by 2.

stem:
Line ℓ in the xy-plane has slope 2 and passes through the point (1, 3). Which of the following points lie on ℓ?

Indicate all such points.
explanation: The equation of ℓ is y − 3 = 2(x − 1), or y = 2x + 1. Test each point: (0, 1), (−1, −1) and (5, 11) satisfy it. (2, 4), (3, 6) and (−2, −5) fit the line y = 2x through the origin, which is the trap of forgetting the intercept.

stem: A square is inscribed in a circle with center O and radius 5, as shown. What is the area of the shaded region?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="95" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><polygon points="217.2,42.8 82.8,42.8 82.8,177.2 217.2,177.2" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="white"/><line x1="150" y1="110" x2="217.2" y2="42.8" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="175.6" y="72.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="140" y="128" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text></svg>
explanation: The diagonal of the square is a diameter, 10, so the square's area is 10²/2 = 50 (or side 5√2 squared). The shaded region is the circle minus the square: 25π − 50 ≈ 28.5. The choice 25π − 25 takes the square's side to be 5, the radius, rather than 5√2.

stem: The total surface area of a cube is 150 square centimeters. What is the volume of the cube, in cubic centimeters?
explanation: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so each face has area 150/6 = 25 and each edge is 5. The volume is 5³ = 125. A common slip is to take the edge as √150 or to divide by 4 faces instead of 6.

stem: What is the perimeter of a semicircular region with radius 6?
explanation: The boundary is half the circle's circumference plus the straight diameter: ½ × 2π × 6 + 12 = 6π + 12. The choice 6π leaves out the diameter, and 6π + 6 adds the radius instead of the diameter.

stem: In the figure, line segment PA is tangent at A to the circle with center O. If OA = 5 and OP = 13, what is the length of PA?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="80" cy="120" r="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="80" y1="120" x2="103.1" y2="64.6" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="103.1" y1="64.6" x2="275" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="80" y1="120" x2="275" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="99.6,72.9 108.2,75.7 111.6,67.4" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="80" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="103.1" y="56.6" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="285" y="126" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="81.5" y="92.3" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="207.5" y="138" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">13</text></svg>
explanation: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so triangle OAP has a right angle at A with hypotenuse OP = 13. Then PA = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12. The choice √194 adds the squares as if OP were a leg, and 8 just subtracts the lengths.

stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (2, −1) and (6, 7) in the xy-plane?
explanation: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (7 − (−1))/(6 − 2) = 8/4 = 2. The choice 1/2 divides the change in x by the change in y, and 3/4 comes from mishandling the negative: (7 − 1)/(6 + 2) = 6/8.

stem:
A cylindrical tank has radius 2 meters and height 3 meters. Which of the following containers have a volume greater than the volume of the tank?

Indicate all such containers.
options: a cube with edges of length 3.5 m
a rectangular box measuring 2 m by 4 m by 5 m
a cylinder with radius 3 m and height 1 m
a cylinder with radius 1 m and height 12 m
a rectangular box measuring 3 m by 3 m by 4 m
explanation: The tank holds π × 2² × 3 = 12π ≈ 37.7 cubic meters. The cube holds 3.5³ ≈ 42.9 and the 2-by-4-by-5 box holds 40, both more. The 3-by-3-by-4 box holds 36, the cylinder of radius 3 and height 1 holds 9π ≈ 28.3, and the cylinder of radius 1 and height 12 holds exactly 12π, which is equal, not greater.

stem: What is the area of the triangle shown in the xy-plane, with vertices at the origin O, (6, 0) and (2, 5)?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="185" x2="285" y2="185" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="205" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="281" y="205" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="54" y="27" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="30" y="203" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><polygon points="40,185 220,185 100,35" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="220" y="205" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(6, 0)</text><text x="136" y="37" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(2, 5)</text></svg>
explanation: Use the side along the x-axis as the base: its length is 6. The height is the vertical distance from (2, 5) to the x-axis, which is 5, no matter where the top vertex sits horizontally. Area = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15. The choice 30 forgets the ½, and 7.5 halves twice.

stem: The figure shows two circles with the same center O and radii 3 and 5. What is the area of the shaded region between them?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="95" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="57" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="white"/><line x1="150" y1="110" x2="207" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="110" x2="150" y2="15" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="178" y="104" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="162" y="38" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="146" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text></svg>
explanation: The shaded ring is the large disk minus the small one: π(5²) − π(3²) = 25π − 9π = 16π. The choice 4π squares the difference of the radii, π(5 − 3)², which is not the same as the difference of the squares.

stem: In a circle, an arc with a central angle of 40° has length 2π. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation: The arc is 40/360 = 1/9 of the circumference, so the circumference is 9 × 2π = 18π. Since circumference = 2πr, r = 9. Answering 18 confuses the diameter with the radius.

stem: A line in the xy-plane has slope −2 and passes through the point (3, 4). What is the x-intercept of the line?
explanation: The equation is y − 4 = −2(x − 3), or y = −2x + 10. The x-intercept is where y = 0: 0 = −2x + 10, so x = 5. The choice 10 is the y-intercept, and −2 comes from a sign slip, writing 4 = 2(3) + b.

stem: The figure shows a region made of a 10-by-4 rectangle with a semicircle attached to each of its shorter sides. What is the area of the region?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="70" y1="78" x2="230" y2="78" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="70" y1="142" x2="230" y2="142" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M 70 78 A 32.0 32.0 0 0 0 70 142" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><path d="M 230 78 A 32.0 32.0 0 0 1 230 142" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="70" y1="78" x2="70" y2="142" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="230" y1="78" x2="230" y2="142" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="150" y="70" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="82" y="116" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
explanation: The rectangle has area 10 × 4 = 40. Each semicircle has diameter 4, so radius 2, and the two semicircles together make one full circle of area π × 2² = 4π. Total: 40 + 4π. The choice 40 + 16π uses the diameter 4 as the radius, and 40 + 8π counts two full circles.

stem:
In the xy-plane, a circle has its center at the origin and radius 5. Which of the following points lie inside the circle (not on it)?

Indicate all such points.
explanation: A point (x, y) is inside the circle when x² + y² < 25. (−4, 2) gives 20, (1, −4.8) gives 1 + 23.04 = 24.04 and (2, −4) gives 20, so they are inside. (3, 4) and (0, −5) give exactly 25, so they are on the circle, not inside. (−3.5, 3.6) gives 12.25 + 12.96 = 25.21, just outside even though each coordinate is less than 5.

stem: A circle has radius 4.
explanation: The circumference is 2π(4) = 8π and the area is π(4²) = 16π, so B is greater. The comparison depends on the radius: 2πr and πr² are equal only when r = 2.

stem: AB is a chord of the circle with center O and radius 6, and AB does not pass through O.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="65.4" y1="79.2" x2="218.9" y2="52.1" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="53.4" y="79.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="230.9" y="52.1" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text></svg>
explanation: The longest chord of a circle is a diameter, here 2 × 6 = 12. AB does not pass through the center, so it is not a diameter and must be shorter than 12. Without that condition, AB could equal 12 and the answer would be (D).

qa: The volume of a cube with edges of length 4
qb: The volume of a rectangular box with dimensions 2, 4 and 8
explanation: The cube's volume is 4³ = 64 and the box's volume is 2 × 4 × 8 = 64. They are equal even though the shapes differ; the box has more surface area (112 against 96), which is a different quantity.

stem: In the xy-plane, the point (a, b) lies on the line y = 2x − 3.
explanation: On the line, b = 2a − 3, so b − a = a − 3. If a = 5, then b = 7 > a; if a = 0, then b = −3 < a; if a = 3, then b = 3 = a. The relationship depends on which point of the line is chosen, so it cannot be determined.

stem:
Points A, B and C lie on a semicircle with center O, and AB is a diameter.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><path d="M 250 120 A 100 100 0 0 0 50 120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="50" y1="120" x2="250" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="50" y1="120" x2="196.9" y2="31.7" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="196.9" y1="31.7" x2="250" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="44" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="256" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="204.9" y="23.7" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text></svg>
explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle, with its sides passing through the ends of a diameter, intercepts an arc of 180°, so it measures half of that: 90°. This holds wherever C is on the arc, so the figure's proportions do not matter.

Solve each for y. 3x + 2y = 6 gives y = −(3/2)x + 3, slope −3/2. 2x + 3y = 6 gives y = −(2/3)x + 2, slope −2/3. Since −1.5 < −0.67, B is greater. The trap is to compare 3/2 and 2/3 without the negative signs, which reverses the answer.

stem: A sector of a circle with radius 6 has a central angle of 60°.
explanation: The sector is 60/360 = 1/6 of the circle, whose area is 36π. So the sector's area is 6π ≈ 18.85, slightly more than 18. Estimating π as 3 would give exactly 18 and the wrong answer (C); π is a little more than 3.14.

qa: The distance between (0, 0) and (5, 12) in the xy-plane
qb: The distance between (1, 1) and (13, 6) in the xy-plane
explanation: A: √(5² + 12²) = 13. B: the changes are 13 − 1 = 12 and 6 − 1 = 5, so the distance is √(12² + 5²) = 13. The quantities are equal; only the size of the changes matters, not where the points are.

stem: Cylinder A has radius 2 and height 6. Cylinder B has radius 3 and height 3.
explanation: Volume is πr²h. A: π × 4 × 6 = 24π. B: π × 9 × 3 = 27π. B is greater because the radius is squared, so a larger radius outweighs a larger height. Adding r + h (8 against 6) points the wrong way.

stem:
Point P lies outside the circle with center O and radius 5, and PT is tangent to the circle at T.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="80" cy="110" r="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="80" y1="110" x2="101.2" y2="53.9" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="101.2" y1="53.9" x2="250" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="80" y1="110" x2="250" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="98,62.3 106.4,65.5 109.6,57" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="80" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="101.2" y="45.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">T</text><text x="260" y="116" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="80.6" y="81.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: Triangle OTP has a right angle at T, so PT = √(OP² − 25). The distance OP is not given. If OP = 6, PT = √11 < 5; if OP = 5√2, PT = 5; if OP = 13, PT = 12 > 5. So the relationship cannot be determined, even though the figure suggests a long tangent.

stem: Line k passes through the origin and the point (3, 4), as shown.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="30" y1="190" x2="285" y2="190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="210" x2="60" y2="15" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="281" y="210" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="74" y="27" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="50" y="208" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><line x1="60" y1="190" x2="186" y2="22" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="114" cy="118" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="148" y="124" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(3, 4)</text><text x="200" y="36" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">k</text></svg>
qa: The y-coordinate of the point on line k whose x-coordinate is 6
explanation: A line through the origin has equation y = mx. Here m = 4/3, so when x = 6, y = (4/3)(6) = 8. Doubling x doubles y on any line through the origin, so (6, 8) is on k. The quantities are equal.

stem: The rectangular box shown has length 5, width 4 and height 3.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="50,90 200,90 200,180 50,180" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="50" y1="90" x2="110" y2="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="200" y1="90" x2="260" y2="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="200" y1="180" x2="260" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="110" y1="45" x2="260" y2="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="260" y1="45" x2="260" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="110" y1="135" x2="110" y2="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="110" y1="135" x2="260" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="50" y1="180" x2="110" y2="135" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="125" y="204" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="36" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="236" y="168" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
qa: The total surface area of the box
explanation: The box has three pairs of faces: 5 × 4, 5 × 3 and 4 × 3, with areas 20, 15 and 12. The total surface area is 2(20 + 15 + 12) = 94, which is greater than 90. Counting each face only once gives 47, and confusing surface area with volume gives 60.

stem: The circumference of circle A is twice the circumference of circle B.
qa: The area of circle A divided by the area of circle B
explanation: Circumference is proportional to the radius, so A's radius is twice B's. Area is proportional to the radius squared, so A's area is 2² = 4 times B's. Since 4 > 2, A is greater. Assuming area scales like circumference gives the trap answer (C).

stem: A circle has radius x, where x > 0.
explanation: Compare 2πx with πx². Dividing both by πx (positive) compares 2 with x. If x < 2 the circumference is larger, if x = 2 they are equal (both 4π), and if x > 2 the area is larger. Since x can be any positive number, the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: In the xy-plane, the point (a, b) lies in quadrant II.
explanation: Quadrant II is the upper left region, where x-coordinates are negative and y-coordinates are positive. So a < 0 < b and B is always greater. Mixing up the quadrant numbering (they go counterclockwise from the upper right) is the usual error.

stem: The line y = mx + 4 passes through the point (2, 0) in the xy-plane.
explanation: Substitute the point: 0 = m(2) + 4, so 2m = −4 and m = −2. The quantities are equal. Plugging the coordinates in the wrong order, 2 = m(0) + 4, leads nowhere, a sign that x and y were swapped.

stem: A rectangular box has a volume of 27.
qa: The total surface area of the box
explanation: If the box is a cube with edge 3, its surface area is 6 × 9 = 54, equal to B. But a 1-by-3-by-9 box also has volume 27, and its surface area is 2(3 + 9 + 27) = 78, greater than B. (No box with this volume has surface area below 54; the cube is the minimum.) Since A can equal or exceed B, the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: Points A, B and C lie on the circle shown. Minor arc AB measures 100°.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="119.2" y1="25.4" x2="81.1" y2="167.9" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="119.2" y1="25.4" x2="218.9" y2="167.9" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="69.1" y="177.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="230.9" y="177.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="119.2" y="17.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text></svg>
explanation: An inscribed angle is half the measure of the arc it intercepts. Angle ACB intercepts minor arc AB of 100°, so it measures 50°, which is greater than 45°. Taking the inscribed angle to equal the arc (100°) also gives A, but for the wrong reason; halving is the step to remember.

stem: A circle has a diameter of 10. A square has sides of length 7.
explanation: The circumference is π × 10 ≈ 31.4 and the square's perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28. A is greater. Using 2πr with r = 10 (that is, mistaking the diameter for the radius) would give 62.8 and the same answer, but would fail on closer comparisons.

stem: A right circular cylinder has radius r and height h, where r > h.
qb: The area of the curved (lateral) surface of the cylinder
explanation: Volume = πr²h and lateral area = 2πrh. Dividing both by πrh compares r with 2. The condition r > h says nothing about r compared with 2: r = 3, h = 1 makes the volume larger (9π against 6π), and r = 1, h = 0.5 makes the lateral area larger (0.5π against π). So the relationship cannot be determined.

qa: The area of a circle inscribed in a square with side 10
qb: The area of a square inscribed in a circle with radius 6
explanation: The inscribed circle has diameter 10, radius 5, so its area is 25π ≈ 78.5. The inscribed square has a diagonal equal to the diameter 12, so its area is 12²/2 = 72. A is greater. Taking the square's side to be 12, or 6, gives 144 or 36 and the wrong answer.

stem: A rectangular sheet of paper measuring 12 inches by 8 inches can be rolled into an open cylinder (no overlap) in two ways: with the 12-inch side forming the circumference, or with the 8-inch side forming the circumference.
qa: The volume of the cylinder when the 12-inch side forms the circumference
qb: The volume of the cylinder when the 8-inch side forms the circumference
explanation: If the circumference is C and the height is H, the radius is C/(2π) and the volume is π(C/(2π))²H = C²H/(4π). A: 12² × 8/(4π) = 1,152/(4π). B: 8² × 12/(4π) = 768/(4π). A is greater: the circumference is squared, so rolling the longer side into the circle wins. The sheet's area is the same both ways, which tempts answer (C).

stem:
Points A, B and C lie on the circle with center O, and AB is a diameter.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="112" r="92" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="59.4" y1="128" x2="240.6" y2="96" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="59.4" y1="128" x2="111.1" y2="28.6" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="111.1" y1="28.6" x2="240.6" y2="96" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="132" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="47.4" y="134" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="252.6" y="94" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="107.1" y="20.6" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text></svg>
explanation: Because AB is a diameter, angle ACB is inscribed in a semicircle and is a right angle. By the Pythagorean theorem, AC² + BC² = AB² wherever C is on the circle (other than A or B). The figure need not be to scale; the right angle follows from the diameter alone.

stem: In the xy-plane, line ℓ is perpendicular to the line 2x − y = 5 and passes through the point (4, 1).
explanation: The line 2x − y = 5 is y = 2x − 5, with slope 2. A perpendicular line has slope −1/2 (negative reciprocal). Through (4, 1): y − 1 = −(1/2)(x − 4), so y = −x/2 + 3, and the y-intercept is 3. Using slope 1/2 (forgetting the sign) gives y-intercept −1, and using −2 gives 9.

stem: A chord of length 12 lies in a circle with radius 10, as shown.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="95" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="93" y1="186" x2="207" y2="186" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="110" x2="150" y2="186" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="150" y1="110" x2="207" y2="186" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="158,186 158,178 150,178" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="102" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="194.5" y="144" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text></svg>
qa: The distance from the center of the circle to the chord
explanation: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects it, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 (a radius) and one leg 6 (half the chord). The other leg, the distance to the chord, is √(100 − 36) = 8, which is greater than 7.5. Using the full chord 12 as a leg makes the problem look impossible (12 > 10).

stem: The shaded region in the xy-plane consists of all points (x, y) with |x| + |y| ≤ 4.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="238,110 150,22 62,110 150,198" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><line x1="30" y1="110" x2="275" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="210" x2="150" y2="12" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="271" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="164" y="24" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="140" y="128" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="242" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="134" y="34" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
qa: The area of the shaded region
qb: The area of a circle with radius 3.2
explanation: The region is a square standing on a corner, with diagonals of length 8 along the axes, so its area is 8 × 8/2 = 32. The circle's area is π × 3.2² = 10.24π ≈ 32.17. B is slightly greater. Rounding π to 3 (which gives 30.72) would flip the answer; with close values, use 3.14.

stem: In the circle with center O and radius 6, angle AOB measures 120°.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="150" cy="125" r="85" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="76.4" y1="167.5" x2="223.6" y2="167.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="125" x2="76.4" y2="167.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="125" x2="223.6" y2="167.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="115" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><text x="64.4" y="173.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="235.6" y="173.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="150" y="151" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">120°</text><text x="192.8" y="138.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text></svg>
qb: The length of minor arc AB
explanation: The arc is 120/360 = 1/3 of the circumference 12π, so it is 4π ≈ 12.57. The perpendicular from O to the chord splits triangle AOB into two 30°-60°-90° triangles with hypotenuse 6, so half the chord is 3√3 and the chord is 6√3 ≈ 10.39. A straight chord is always shorter than the arc it cuts off.

stem: The point (p, q) lies on the circle x² + y² = 25 in the xy-plane, and p > 3.
explanation: On the circle, q² = 25 − p². Since 3 < p ≤ 5, p² > 9, so q² < 16 and |q| < 4. The point (3, 4) has |q| = 4 exactly, but it is excluded because p must be greater than 3.

stem: The rectangular box shown has a square base with side s, height h and a volume of 100.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="70,80 180,80 180,180 70,180" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="70" y1="80" x2="125" y2="40" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="180" y1="80" x2="235" y2="40" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="180" y1="180" x2="235" y2="140" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="125" y1="40" x2="235" y2="40" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="235" y1="40" x2="235" y2="140" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="125" y1="140" x2="125" y2="40" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="125" y1="140" x2="235" y2="140" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="70" y1="180" x2="125" y2="140" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="125" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">s</text><text x="240" y="166" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">s</text><text x="56" y="135" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">h</text></svg>
explanation: If the base side is s, the height is 100/s². With s = 5 the height is 4 (less than s); with s = 2 the height is 25 (more than s); with s = ∛100 the box is a cube and they are equal. So the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: In the xy-plane, the distance between the points (−3, k) and (5, 2) is 10.
explanation: The horizontal change is 8, so 8² + (k − 2)² = 10², giving (k − 2)² = 36 and k − 2 = ±6. So k = 8 or k = −4. One value is greater than 0 and one is less, so the relationship cannot be determined. Taking only the positive square root is the trap.

stem:
In the figure, the circle with center P has radius 5, the circle with center Q has radius 3, and PQ = 10.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><circle cx="75" cy="110" r="45" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="255" cy="110" r="27" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="75" y1="110" x2="255" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="75" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="255" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">Q</text></svg>
qa: The shortest distance between a point on the circle with center P and a point on the circle with center Q
explanation: The closest points lie on segment PQ: from P go 5 to reach the first circle, and from Q go 3 to reach the second. What remains between them is 10 − 5 − 3 = 2. Any other pair of points is farther apart, because a straight path along PQ is the shortest route between the centers.

stem: In the xy-plane, O is the origin, A is the point (4, 0), and P is a point on the line y = 3.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="30" y1="180" x2="285" y2="180" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="205" x2="60" y2="30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="281" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="74" y="42" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="50" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><line x1="30" y1="84" x2="285" y2="84" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polygon points="60,180 188,180 236,84" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="188" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A(4, 0)</text><text x="236" y="76" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="110" y="78" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="start">y = 3</text></svg>
explanation: Use OA, of length 4, as the base. The height is the vertical distance from P to the x-axis, which is 3 for every point on the line y = 3. So the area is always ½ × 4 × 3 = 6, wherever P is, even when the triangle leans far to one side.

stem: The radius of a right circular cylinder is multiplied by k, and its height is divided by k, where k > 0.
qa: The volume of the new cylinder
qb: The volume of the original cylinder
explanation: The new volume is π(kr)²(h/k) = k × πr²h, so it is k times the original. If k > 1 the new cylinder is larger, if k = 1 nothing changes, and if 0 < k < 1 it is smaller. Since k is only known to be positive, the relationship cannot be determined. Assuming the changes cancel (they would only for a box scaled the same way) leads to (C).

stem: The figure shows a circle inscribed in a square with side length 2. The shaded region lies between one corner of the square and the circle.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><path d="M 70 30 L 150.0 30 A 80.0 80.0 0 0 0 70 110.0 Z" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><polygon points="70,30 230,30 230,190 70,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="150" cy="110" r="80" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="210" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">2</text></svg>
qa: The area of the shaded region
explanation: The circle has radius 1 and area π. The four corner regions together have area 4 − π ≈ 0.858, and by symmetry the shaded one is a quarter of that, (4 − π)/4 ≈ 0.215, which is less than 0.25. Estimating π as 3 gives exactly 0.25 and the wrong answer (C).

stem: A circle with radius r and a square with side s have equal areas.
explanation: From πr² = s², s = r√π. The circumference is 2πr ≈ 6.28r and the square's perimeter is 4r√π ≈ 4 × 1.772 × r ≈ 7.09r. So the square has the longer boundary: for a fixed area, a circle encloses it with the shortest possible perimeter.

stem: A line in the xy-plane passes through the point (1, 2) and has negative slope.
explanation: With slope m < 0, the line is y = m(x − 1) + 2, so the y-intercept is 2 − m and the x-intercept is 1 − 2/m. For m = −1 both are 3; for m = −2 they are 4 and 2; for m = −1/2 they are 2.5 and 5. The relationship depends on the slope, so it cannot be determined.

stem: An arc of circle A with a central angle of 60° has the same length as an arc of circle B with a central angle of 45°.
explanation: Arc length is (angle/360) × 2πr, so (60/360) × 2πr_A = (45/360) × 2πr_B, which gives 60r_A = 45r_B and r_B = (4/3)r_A. Circle B needs a larger radius to make a smaller angle cut off the same length. Thinking the larger angle must belong to the larger circle gives the reverse answer.

stem: A rectangular box has dimensions 2, 3 and 6.
qa: The length of the longest line segment that fits inside the box
explanation: The longest segment joins opposite corners through the interior: √(2² + 3² + 6²) = √49 = 7. The quantities are equal. The longest face diagonal, √(3² + 6²) = √45 ≈ 6.7, is shorter and would lead to the answer B.

stem: In the xy-plane, a triangle has vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (a, b), where b > 0. The area of the triangle is 12.
explanation: With base 6 on the x-axis, the area is ½ × 6 × b = 12, so b = 4. That fixes the height but not the horizontal position: a can be any number, such as 0, 4 or 10. The trap is to compute b = 4 and compare it with Quantity B as if it were a.

stem: A circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle with side 6, as shown.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,39.1 60,195 240,195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="150" cy="143" r="52" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="215" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text></svg>
qb: Half the area of the triangle
explanation: The triangle's height is 3√3, and the center of the inscribed circle is one third of the way up, so the radius is √3. The circle's area is 3π ≈ 9.42. The triangle's area is (√3/4) × 36 = 9√3 ≈ 15.59, so half of it is about 7.79. A is greater: the circle fills about 60% of the triangle.

stem: A circle has a diameter of 14. What is the area of the circle?
explanation: The radius is half the diameter, 7, so the area is π × 7² = 49π. The choice 196π uses the diameter as the radius, and 14π is the circumference.

stem: Which of the following points lies in quadrant IV of the xy-plane?
explanation: Quadrants are numbered counterclockwise from the upper right. Quadrant IV is the lower right, where x > 0 and y < 0, so (3, −2) is the answer. (0, −2) lies on the y-axis, which belongs to no quadrant, and (−3, −2) is in quadrant III.

stem: What is the volume of the rectangular box shown, with dimensions 5, 3 and 2?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="50,80 200,80 200,170 50,170" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="50" y1="80" x2="120" y2="30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="200" y1="80" x2="270" y2="30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="200" y1="170" x2="270" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="30" x2="270" y2="30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="270" y1="30" x2="270" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="120" x2="120" y2="30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="120" y1="120" x2="270" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="50" y1="170" x2="120" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="125" y="194" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="36" y="130" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="246" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">2</text></svg>
explanation: The volume of a rectangular box is length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. Adding the dimensions (10) or finding the area of one face (15) are the usual slips.

stem: A circle has a diameter of 9.
explanation: The radius is half the diameter: 9/2 = 4.5. The quantities are equal.

stem: A circle has radius 1.
explanation: The area is π × 1² = π ≈ 3.14, which is less than 3.2. Rounding π up to 3.2 or confusing it with 22/7 ≈ 3.143 does not change the answer here, but rounding to 3.2 would wrongly suggest (C).

stem: What is the total surface area of a cube with edges of length 3?
explanation: A cube has 6 square faces, each with area 3 × 3 = 9, so the surface area is 6 × 9 = 54. The choice 27 is the volume (3³), and 9 is the area of a single face.

stem: Points A(2, 5) and B(2, −1) are shown in the xy-plane.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="30" y1="150" x2="270" y2="150" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="205" x2="90" y2="25" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="266" y="170" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="104" y="37" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="80" y="168" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><circle cx="130" cy="50" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="130" cy="170" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="170" y="56" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A(2, 5)</text><text x="176" y="176" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B(2, −1)</text></svg>
explanation: A and B have the same x-coordinate, so AB is vertical and its length is the difference of the y-coordinates: 5 − (−1) = 6, which is greater than 5. Subtracting 5 − 1 = 4 ignores the negative sign.

stem: A circular rug has a radius of 3 meters. What is its area, in square meters?
explanation: Area = πr² = π × 3² = 9π square meters. The choice 36π uses the diameter 6 in place of the radius, and 18π multiplies 2 × 9 instead of squaring.

stem: The figure shows a square with side length 8 and a quarter circle centered at the lower left corner of the square with radius 8. What is the area of the shaded region?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><path d="M 70 30 L 240 30 L 240 200 A 170 170 0 0 0 70 30 Z" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><polygon points="70,200 240,200 240,30 70,30" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><path d="M 70 30 A 170 170 0 0 1 240 200" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="155" y="216" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text></svg>
explanation: The quarter circle has area ¼ × π × 8² = 16π, and the square has area 64. The shaded region is what is left: 64 − 16π ≈ 13.7. The choice 64 − 4π uses the radius 4, and 64 − 8π takes half instead of a quarter of the circle.

stem:
Which of the following points in the xy-plane are at a distance of exactly 5 from the point (1, 1)?

Indicate all such points.
explanation: Check whether (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 25. (4, 5): 9 + 16 = 25. (−2, −3): 9 + 16 = 25. (−4, 1): 25 + 0 = 25. (6, 2) gives 26, (1, −5) gives 36 and (3, 6) gives 29, so they are not at distance 5. The 3-4-5 pattern is a quick way to spot the right points.

stem: A line in the xy-plane passes through the points (0, 3) and (k, 0), where k ≠ 0.
explanation: The slope is (0 − 3)/(k − 0) = −3/k. If k = 3 the slope is −1; if k = 6 it is −1/2 (greater than −1); if k = 1 it is −3 (less than −1); and if k is negative the slope is positive. So the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: In the figure, O is the center of the circle and angle ACB measures 40°.

explanation: The central angle AOB and the inscribed angle ACB intercept the same arc AB, and a central angle is twice the inscribed angle: x = 2 × 40 = 80. Since 80 < 85, B is greater. Halving instead of doubling gives 20, which leads to the same answer here only by luck.

stem: A cube-shaped container with inside edge 6 inches is full of water. All the water is poured into an empty cylindrical container with inside radius 3 inches, and none spills. How deep, in inches, is the water in the cylinder?
explanation: The water's volume is 6³ = 216 cubic inches. In the cylinder it fills π × 3² × h = 9πh, so h = 216/(9π) = 24/π ≈ 7.6 inches. The choice 6/π uses the diameter 6 as the radius (216/(36π)), and 12/π divides by 18π, the area 2πr instead of πr².

stem: A sector of a circle with radius 6 has an area of 12π. What is the measure, in degrees, of the central angle of the sector?
explanation: The whole circle has area π × 6² = 36π. The sector is 12π/36π = 1/3 of the circle, so its central angle is 1/3 of 360°, which is 120°. Comparing the sector with the circumference (12π) instead of the area would wrongly give 360°.

qa: The number of points at which the circle intersects the x-axis
explanation: The center is 3 units above the x-axis and the radius is 4, which is more than 3, so the circle crosses the x-axis at exactly 2 points. A circle and a line can meet in at most 2 points, so Quantity A can never reach 3.

stem: What is the area of the parallelogram shown in the xy-plane, with vertices O(0, 0), (4, 0), (5, 3) and (1, 3)?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="30" y1="170" x2="285" y2="170" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="200" x2="60" y2="25" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="281" y="190" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="74" y="37" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="50" y="188" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><polygon points="60,170 180,170 210,80 90,80" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="180" y="190" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(4, 0)</text><text x="220" y="72" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(5, 3)</text><text x="86" y="72" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(1, 3)</text></svg>
explanation: The base along the x-axis has length 4, and the height is the vertical distance between the parallel sides, 3. Area = base × height = 4 × 3 = 12. The choice 6 halves it as if it were a triangle, and 15 multiplies 5 × 3, using an x-coordinate as the base.

stem: Cylinder X has radius 4 and height 2. Cylinder Y has radius 2 and height 8.
explanation: X: π × 4² × 2 = 32π. Y: π × 2² × 8 = 32π. They are equal: halving the radius divides the volume by 4, which the fourfold height exactly makes up for. Squaring the height instead of the radius (π × 4 × 2² against π × 2 × 8²) is a common slip that would make Y look far larger.

stem: A circle is inscribed in a square, and the square is inscribed in a larger circle. What is the ratio of the area of the larger circle to the area of the smaller circle?
explanation: If the square has side 2, the small circle has radius 1 (half the side) and the large circle has radius √2 (half the diagonal 2√2). The areas are in the ratio (√2)² : 1² = 2 : 1. The choice √2 : 1 is the ratio of the radii, not the areas.

stem:
Line ℓ in the xy-plane passes through the point (2, 3) and does not pass through quadrant III. Which of the following could be the slope of ℓ?

Indicate all such slopes.
explanation: The line is y = m(x − 2) + 3. If m > 0, then far enough to the left (x very negative) y becomes negative too, so the line enters quadrant III, however small m is (for m = 1/4 that happens once x < −10). If m = 0 the line is y = 3, and if m < 0, then for every x < 0, y = m(x − 2) + 3 > 3 > 0. So exactly the slopes −3, −1/2 and 0 work.

stem: A square and an equilateral triangle are each inscribed in a circle with radius r.
explanation: The square's diagonal is the diameter 2r, so its area is (2r)²/2 = 2r². The triangle's side is r√3 (its height is 1.5r, since the center is two thirds of the way down from a vertex), so its area is (√3/4)(3r²) ≈ 1.30r². The square is larger for every r.

stem:
The point (a, b) lies on the circle x² + y² = 25 in quadrant II, as shown.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="40" y1="115" x2="260" y2="115" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="215" x2="150" y2="15" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="256" y="135" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="164" y="27" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y</text><text x="140" y="133" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">O</text><circle cx="150" cy="115" r="85" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="101.2" cy="45.4" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="73.2" y="37.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(a, b)</text></svg>
explanation: In quadrant II, a < 0 < b, and a² + b² = 25. If the point is (−3, 4), a + b = 1 > 0; if it is (−4, 3), a + b = −1 < 0; and at (−5/√2, 5/√2) the sum is 0. Since the figure is not drawn to scale, the position of the point cannot be read from it, so the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: Three faces of a rectangular box that meet at one corner have areas 12, 15 and 20.
explanation: If the edges are l, w and h, then lw = 12, wh = 15 and lh = 20. Multiplying, (lwh)² = 12 × 15 × 20 = 3,600, so lwh = 60. (The edges are 4, 3 and 5.) Multiplying the three areas without taking the square root gives 3,600, and adding them gives 47; neither is the volume.

stem: Two circles, each with radius 3, have centers P and Q, and each circle passes through the center of the other. What is the area of the shaded region common to both circles?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><path d="M 150 58.0 A 60 60 0 0 1 150 162.0 A 60 60 0 0 1 150 58.0 Z" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><circle cx="120" cy="110" r="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="180" cy="110" r="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="120" cy="110" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><circle cx="180" cy="110" r="3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="116" y="132" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="184" y="132" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">Q</text></svg>
explanation: Join P and Q to the two intersection points: all four segments are radii of length 3, and PQ = 3, so they form two equilateral triangles and each center sees the shaded region under a 120° angle. The part of the region on one side of the common chord is a 120° sector (area 9π/3 = 3π) minus a triangle with sides 3, 3 and 3√3 (area 9√3/4). Doubling gives 6π − 9√3/2. The choice 3π − 9√3/4 is only half the region.

stem: In the xy-plane, how many points with integer coordinates lie on the circle x² + y² = 25?
explanation: We need integer pairs with x² + y² = 25. The four axis points (±5, 0) and (0, ±5) work, and so do all sign combinations of (3, 4) and (4, 3): (±3, ±4) and (±4, ±3), 8 more. Total 4 + 8 = 12. Counting only the first quadrant (3, 4) and (4, 3), or forgetting the axis points, gives too few.

stem: A closed cylindrical can, shown, has a volume of 54π cubic inches, and its height h equals its diameter d. What is the total surface area of the can, in square inches?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><ellipse cx="150" cy="50" rx="62" ry="18" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="88" y1="50" x2="88" y2="175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="212" y1="50" x2="212" y2="175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M 88 175 A 62 18 0 0 0 212 175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><path d="M 88 175 A 62 18 0 0 1 212 175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="88" y1="196" x2="212" y2="196" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="214" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">d</text><text x="230" y="117" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">h</text></svg>
explanation: With h = 2r, the volume is πr²(2r) = 2πr³ = 54π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3, h = 6. The two circular ends have area 2 × 9π = 18π and the curved side has area 2πrh = 2π × 3 × 6 = 36π. Total: 54π. The choice 36π is only the curved surface, and 45π counts one end.
